blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Vision-language models (VLMs) achieve remarkable performance on 2D medical images, such as X-rays or pathology images, while 3D VLMs that directly process CT/MRI volumes lag behind due to limited 3D training data and the predominance of 2D foundation architectures. To leverage powerful 2D VLMs for analyzing medical volumes, which contain hundreds of slices, it is therefore necessary to focus only on those few slices, which are diagnostically relevant. To enable such a prioritization, we propose XGLASS, a method that transfers medical expertise from 2D X-rays to 3D CT for task-aware slice prioritization. XGLASS uses disease-conditioned importance maps derived from language-aligned radiologist gaze on X-rays and spatially aligns them with coronal CT projections, bringing gaze priors and CT content into a shared 2D representation. The fused gaze-prior/CT projection is then used to predict a disease-specific ordering of axial slices, prioritizing diagnostically relevant slices. XGLASS significantly improves budgeted retrieval over 2D and 3D-native baselines, achieving a top-10 hit rate up to 75.9% for the best-performing disease. In practice, this means that after inspecting only the top 10 slices (4.17% of a 240-slice scan), XGLASS identifies a diagnostically relevant slice in more than 75% of cases. For downstream slice-wise finding classification, an XGLASS-selected 30-slice candidate set reduces model calls by 87.5% while improving F1 by 11.3 percentage points over all-slice inference, 4.2 points over the strongest 2D selector, and remains competitive with 3D-native selectors while requiring up to 130.8 times less time and 10.9 times less GPU memory per finding, supporting its use as a lightweight preselector for volumetric CT analysis. The code and pretrained checkpoint are available on https://github.com/michaelgloeckler/XGLASS.
blocks.zh: 视觉语言模型(VLMs)在X射线或病理影像等2D医学图像上取得了出众的性能,而直接处理CT/MRI卷的3D VLM由于3D训练数据有限和2D基础架构占主导地位而滞后. 为了利用强大的2D VLM来分析含有上百个切片的医学卷,因此,必须只关注那些与诊断相关的少数切片. 为了能够确定这种优先次序,我们建议采用XGLASS,将医疗专门知识从2D X光转移到3D CT,以便确定任务的优先次序。 XGLASS使用基于语言相通的放射学家对X射线的视线所绘制的以疾病为条件的重要地图,并在空间上将其与日冕CT的预测相匹配,将视线前传和CT内容带入一个共享的2D代表. 然后使用引信的凝视先入为出/CT投影来预测轴切片因疾病而异的顺序,优先排列诊断相关切片. XGLASS大大改进了2D和3D本土基线的预算检索,使表现最好的疾病达到最高为75.9%的上-10个命中率. 在实践中,这意味着XGLASS只检查了前10个切片(240-切片扫描的4.17%)后,在超过75%的病例中识别出一个诊断相关的切片. 在下游切入法中,XGLAS选取的30个切入法选取法将模式调用率减少87.5%,同时将F1比全切入法提高11.3%,比最强的2D选取法提高4.2分,与3D选取法保持竞争力,同时每选取法需要最多130.8倍的时间和10.9倍的GPU内存,支持其作为轻量级预选器来进行体积CT分析. 密码和事先经过训练的检查站可在https://github.com/michaelgloeckler/XGLASS上查阅。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Vision-language models (VLMs) have recently enabled remarkable progress in computer vision, in tasks such as zero-/few-shot recognition, retrieval, and visual question answering (VQA), largely driven by the abundance of real-world image-text pairs [ 1 , 2 , 8 , 37 , 38 , 33 ] . Analogously, the release of large paired medical datasets [ 17 , 18 , 7 ] has catalyzed medical adaptations, leading to CLIP-style medical contrastive models [ 42 , 25 , 49 , 46 , 47 ] and medical VLMs [ 31 , 35 , 24 ] capable of report generation, diagnosis, and medical VQA. Alongside these models, a growing ecosystem of 2D medical datasets has emerged, such as closed- and open-ended VQA benchmarks targeting medical questions [ 26 , 15 , 23 , 48 ] . However, the majority of these resources contains 2D medical images, such as x-ray or pathology slides. When CT or MRI appear in those datasets, they are typically represented by single, diagnostically relevant slices that were manually extracted by experts, rather than complete 3D volumes [ 15 , 23 , 26 ] . This results in a mismatch between dataset availability and diagnostic requirements, since core diagnostic modalities, such as CT or MRI, are inherently 3D. Applying 2D VLMs directly to complete CT volumes would require processing every axial slice independently, which is computationally expensive and often inefficient because most slices are redundant or irrelevant to a queried finding. In practice, downstream applications such as slice-wise VLM screening, computer-aided detection (CAD), and 2D dataset curation benefit from compact disease-conditioned candidate sets rather than exhaustive all-slice inference [ 41 ] . Motivated by this gap between predominantly 2D VLMs and the 3D nature of clinical imaging, we propose X-Ray, Gaze and Language Assisted Slice Sequencing (XGLASS), a lightweight method that transfers radiologist gaze-language priors learned on chest X-rays (CXRs) to rank axial CT slices by diagnostic relevance in a disease-conditioned manner. XGLASS effectively regresses a continuous, 240-dimensional relevance profile over axial slices, enabling relevance ranking, top- k k slice extraction, and importance-based traversal for retrieval or VLM conditioning. Empirically, XGLASS improves budgeted slice retrieval over 2D and 3D-native baselines, reaching 75.9% Hit@10 for the best-performing disease, while downstream VLM screening shows that XGLASS-selected candidate sets reduce model calls by 87.5% and improve F1 by up to 11.3 points over all-slice inference. To this end, we make the following contributions: • We introduce disease-conditioned importance maps from medical expert knowledge collected through x-ray eye-tracking data and synchronized speech recordings. • We propose XGLASS, a lightweight 2D-to-3D cross-modal model that transfers these priors to CT projections and predicts disease-specific axial slice relevance scores. • We evaluate XGLASS against 2D and 3D-native baselines, showing significantly better budgeted retrieval, substantially lower inference cost, and downstream F1 gains while reducing model calls by 87.5%.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: Eye-tracking in medical imaging. Radiologist eye-tracking provides implicit supervision of diagnostic search behavior and has been used to study visual expertise, diagnostic performance, and attention allocation [ 22 , 39 , 12 , 20 ] . Recent CXR datasets such as REFLACX and MIMIC-Eye link gaze with report transcripts [ 4 , 16 , 19 ] , enabling gaze-guided localization, attention steering, and multimodal alignment [ 5 , 28 , 21 ] . In contrast, eye-tracking data for 3D CT remain scarce: CT-Scangaze [ 32 ] provides 3D scanpaths with dictation transcripts, but its limited number of only 57 distinct scanpath–report pairs makes it unsuitable for deriving stable disease-specific importance maps.
blocks.zh: 医学成像中的眼跟踪. 放射学家眼跟踪为诊断搜索行为提供了隐含的监督,并被用于研究视觉专业知识,诊断性能,以及注意力分配[22,39,12,20]. 最近的CXR数据集,如REFLACX和MIMIC-Eye将目视与报告记录 [4、16、19] 相连接,使目视能够指导本地化、注意力引导和多模式对接 [5、28、21]。 相比之下,3D CT的目光跟踪数据仍然很少:CT-Scangaze[32] 提供了3D扫描路径的口述记录,但其数量有限,只有57个不同的扫描路径-报告对等,使其不适合绘制稳定的针对特定疾病的重要地图。

blocks.en: Figure 1 : Overview of the XGLASS Pipeline. Given a chest CT and chest X-ray eye-tracking data with matching report transcripts as input, we first normalize CT volumes and compute coronal CT intensity projections, while also matching gaze and disease mentions to derive disease-conditioned importance maps. These importance maps are spatially aligned to the CT projection and fused via alpha blending. The gaze-enriched intensity projection is input to the ViT-based regression head trained with MSE to predict a slice-importance vector. For inference, the model uses the precomputed importance map for the desired disease fused with the CT intensity projection and outputs a disease-specific relevance ordering of axial slices, ranking diagnostically important slices at the top.

blocks.en: Slice selection for 3D medical imaging. CT and MRI interpretation requires scrolling through volumetric slices, making slice selection useful for reducing redundancy and enabling 2D models to process 3D data. Vote-MI [ 41 ] selects representative slices from 2D features, but remains unsupervised, not disease-conditioned, and requires encoding all slices before selection, increasing computational cost. Although CT reading differs from CXR interpretation through slice drilling and z-axis-ordered search [ 12 ] , our CXR–CT gaze-prior comparison in Supplementary Sec. B.4 shows correlated superior–inferior disease-attention profiles across modalities ( r = 0.65 r{=}0.65 – 0.96 0.96 ), supporting XGLASS’s transfer of 2D gaze priors for CT axial slice sequencing.
blocks.zh: 3D医疗成像的切片选择. CT和核磁共振解释需要通过卷片来滚动,使切片选择对减少冗余有用并使得2D模型能够处理3D数据. Vote-MI [41] 从2D特性中选择具有代表性的切片,但依然不受监督,而不是疾病条件限制,在选择前需要对所有切片进行编码,增加了计算成本. 尽管CT读取与CXR通过切片钻探和z轴序搜索的判读不同[12],但我们的CXR-CT在"补充sec"中的凝视-先入为主的比较。 B.4 显示了各种模式之间相关优异的-恶性疾病观察剖面(r = 0.65 r{=}0.65– 0.96 0.96),支持XGLASS为CT轴切片测序转移2D凝视前科。

blocks.en: 3.1 Disease-Conditioned Importance Maps
blocks.zh: 3.1 有疾病影响的重要地图

blocks.en: A central component of XGLASS is the construction of disease-specific 2D importance maps G G that capture how expert radiologists navigate through chest X-rays. To obtain these priors, we leverage the eye-tracking data paired with dictated report texts, available in the REFLACX dataset [ 4 ] . For disease filtering for each report transcript, we use custom regular expressions similar to SARLE [ 11 ] to identify disease-specific mentions in the spoken text. The timestamps associated with these textual matches define a temporal window during which the radiologist was verbally describing the relevant findings. Prior work in psycholinguistics shows that speakers’ gaze reliably anticipates verbal articulation by more than one second, motivating the inclusion of a short pre-speech buffer on the order of 1–1.5 s [ 14 ] . Given the cognitive load and visual search demands of CT interpretation, we included a slightly longer pre-speech buffer of 2 s to ensure we capture all relevant fixation points. blocks.zh: 3.2 CT 体积预测

blocks.en: Our method takes two complementary sources of supervision: pre-computed, disease-specific 2D gaze importance maps derived from radiologist eye-tracking on chest X-rays using the REFLACX dataset [ 4 ] , and a volumetric CT dataset that shares matching disease findings and therefore ReXGroundingCT [ 3 ] is to our knowledge the largest CT dataset that fulfills our requirements. To project a given CT volume into the disease-conditioned importance map domain, we first need to perform an intensity projection followed by a projection window normalization.

blocks.en: Our model builds on a ViT-B/16 backbone with AugReg ImageNet-21k pretraining [ 10 ] , which processes the fused representation of the disease-conditioned importance map G G and projected CT volume P P . To adapt the network from classification to slice-importance regression, we replace the original classification head with a lightweight two-layer MLP that outputs a fixed-length vector y ^ ∈ ℝ Z target \hat{y}\in\mathbb{R}^{Z_{\text{target}}} ( Z target = 240 Z_{\text{target}}=240 ). A final sigmoid activation constrains all predictions to the range [ 0 , 1 ] [0,1] , matching the normalized ground-truth slice–area profiles. The model receives a 3-channel 224 × 224 224\times 224 image initialized with a coronal CT intensity projection P P , replicated across all three input channels. The corresponding disease-specific importance map G G is then spatially scaled to the chest bounding-box region in the projection and blended into the red channel with an opacity coefficient α \alpha , while the green and blue channels remain unchanged. This channel-wise injection allows the ViT to process the anatomical projection and gaze-derived prior jointly in a single forward pass, enabling the model to estimate slice relevance directly from the fused representation. During training, the model obtains as input the fused G G and P P image, and learns to regress the ground-truth slice–area vector derived in Sec. 3.2 . For each input image, the network outputs y ^ ∈ [ 0 , 1 ] 240 \hat{y}\in[0,1]^{240} and is optimized using MSE loss between y ^ \hat{y} and the corresponding normalized ground-truth vector y y . We train the full model end-to-end using the AdamW optimizer with a differential learning rate schedule, assigning a higher learning rate to the regression head ( 1 × 10 − 4 1\times 10^{-4} ) and a lower rate to the ViT backbone ( 1 × 10 − 5 1\times 10^{-5} ). Training is performed with a batch size of 16. This setup preserves the pretrained backbone’s representational capacity while allowing the head to adapt to the slice-importance regression task.

blocks.en: We benchmark XGLASS against the state-of-the-art slice selection method Vote-MI [ 41 ] , a BioMedCLIP-based slice-wise retrieval baseline [ 47 ] , heuristic and prior-only baselines, two 3D-native baselines [ 6 , 9 ] , and a gaze-free variant of our model. Only the gaze-prior baseline and gaze-guided XGLASS use REFLACX gaze information; BioMedCLIP, 3D Merlin + MLP, 3D U-Net, and XGLASS are disease-conditioned, while XGLASS (w/out gaze), Vote-MI, Gaussian Centered, and Random are disease-agnostic. Gaze prior only ranks slices using only the disease-specific gaze-derived superior–inferior profile, without patient-specific CT input, serving as a control for static anatomical prior effects. Vote-MI was originally proposed for brain MRI; we follow its preprocessing and two-stage slice-selection procedure, but adapt it to thoracic CT by replacing the original feature extractor with MedVAE [ 40 ] , a medical foundation model, and convert the selected representatives into continuous slice scores for fair metric-based comparison. BioMedCLIP is used as a slice-wise image–text retrieval baseline. For each CT-condition pair, we encode all axial slices with the BioMedCLIP image encoder and the queried disease text with the text encoder, and then rank slices by image–text cosine similarity to obtain a disease-conditioned 240-dimensional relevance score vector. Full prompt and implementation details are provided in Supplementary Sec. G.1 . For the 3D-native model comparisons, 3D Merlin + MLP uses a frozen Merlin volumetric encoder [ 6 ] followed by a disease-conditioned MLP trained to regress the same 240-dimensional slice-relevance target as XGLASS, ands 3D U-Net [ 9 ] uses a 3D U-Net encoder trained from scratch on ReXGroundingCT with a slice-regression head for the same targets. Further implementation details for both 3D baselines are provided in Supplementary Sec. G.2 . XGLASS (w/o gaze cues) uses the identical backbone, projections, loss, and training as XGLASS but disables the gaze blend ( α = 0 \alpha{=}0 ), isolating the architecture without disease-specific importance priors. Gaussian Centered places a Gaussian bump over slice indices with fractional width σ frac \sigma_{\text{frac}} , yielding higher scores near the mid-thorax, and Random draws an independent score for each slice from Uniform ⁡ [ 0 , 1 ] \mathrm{Uniform}[0,1] to reflect chance performance. All methods output a 240-dimensional score vector per study and are evaluated with the same metrics (ROC-AUC, Spearman’s ρ \rho , Hit@K, and AR@K), as described in Section 4.1 .

blocks.en: 4.3 Overall Performance
blocks.zh: 4.3 总体业绩

blocks.en: Table 1 shows that gaze-guided XGLASS outperforms the 2D baselines across all reported metrics, with paired bootstrap intervals indicating significant gains in Hit@5, Hit@10, AUC, and Spearman’s ρ \rho . The native 3D baselines are competitive on global ranking metrics, with 3D U-Net achieving the highest AUC and Spearman’s ρ \rho point estimates and 3D Merlin achieving the highest Hit@1 and AR@10 point estimates. Despite operating on the full CT volume, the 3D baselines do not translate their small non-significant advantages in Hit@1 and global ranking into reliable slice retrieval and XGLASS remains significantly better on Hit@5 and Hit@10, the most relevant metrics for prioritizing a compact inspection set. Figure 3 further shows that XGLASS reaches the first diagnostically relevant slice earlier and more consistently than all baselines. In the coverage analysis (Figure 3 ), the 3D baselines become competitive, but together with their later first-hit distributions in Figure 3 , it suggests that the 3D models recover dense relevant regions once the correct location is found, but are less reliable at finding that location in every case. A case-level Miss@10 analysis supports this interpretation: Merlin and 3D U-Net miss the early inspection budget in 190/316 and 202/316 cases, respectively, compared with only 138/316 missed cases for XGLASS, indicating that their slightly higher Hit@1, AR@10, and global-ranking point estimates do not translate into more reliable compact-budget retrieval. For clinical use cases, reliably surfacing at least one diagnostic slice within the inspected budget is more valuable than dense coverage only after successful localization, making XGLASS more suitable for practical slice selection, especially since it also requires 34.8 × \times less inference time and 6.5 × \times less GPU memory than Merlin, and 130.8 × \times less time and 10.9 × \times less memory than U-Net.

blocks.en: 4.3.1 Disease-specific Performance
blocks.zh: 4.3.1 特定疾病 业绩

blocks.en: The per-category trends in Table 2 align with typical anatomical distributions. Consolidation and Pleural abnormalities are often gravity-dependent and cluster in posterior lower lobes, producing a relatively narrow and predictable band along the z z -axis. This yields the highest AUC/ ρ \rho and strong Hit@K performance. Ground-glass opacities are frequently diffuse and extend across adjacent slices, which lifts mid- to higher- K K retrieval (e.g., Hit@10) but softens global ranking metrics. In contrast, lung nodules/masses are small, sparse, and spatially unpredictable along the z z -axis, which reduces the chance that the very top-ranked slices contain a hit and depresses global rank agreement. Thus, lung nodules are relatively less suited to our approach due to their small size and variable location, characteristics that also make them challenging for slice-selection methods in general. When evaluated only on the lung-nodule subset, XGLASS achieves the strongest Hit@K and AUC, showing that despite performing worse than on other diseases, it still provides the best slice prioritization (Supplementary Sec. D ). Taken together, these findings indicate that XGLASS learns disease-specific z z -axis priors similar to radiologist behaviour, prioritizes anatomically informative regions, and therefore performs best for conditions with consistent spatial distributions such as consolidations.

blocks.en: 4.3.2 Computational Efficiency
blocks.zh: 4.3.2 计算效率

blocks.en: XGLASS contains approximately 86M parameters and is trained on a single 2D projection per CT study. On an NVIDIA RTX 4080, one training epoch over 2,512 projections with batch size 16 takes 62.2 s, corresponding to roughly 40 samples/s, with approximately 3 GB peak GPU memory. Early stopping on validation loss consistently selects checkpoints after 6–8 epochs, yielding a complete training run in under 10 minutes. At inference time, XGLASS processes a full CT study, including intensity projection, in approximately 0.025 s per finding (0.150 s for all findings) with an estimated cost of 33.7 GFLOPs and 0.34 GB memory. In comparison, Vote-MI requires 7.51 s and approximately 116.33 TFLOPs per CT, while slice-wise BioMedCLIP requires 1.40 s and approximately 8.09 TFLOPs per CT. The 3D Merlin and U-Net baselines require 0.87 s and 3.27 s per finding, respectively, with 2.21 GB and 3.72 GB peak inference memory, making them 34.8 × \times /130.8 × \times slower and 6.5 × \times /10.9 × \times more memory-intensive than XGLASS. Overall, XGLASS is orders of magnitude cheaper than slice-wise 2D baselines and substantially faster and more memory-efficient than the 3D baselines, making local retraining on commodity GPUs feasible for institutions with private clinical data.

blocks.en: 4.3.3 Downstream Slice-wise VLM Screening
blocks.zh: 4.3.3 下游切片VLM 筛选

blocks.en: We evaluate XGLASS as a disease-conditioned pre-filter for slice-wise VLM screening with 2D VLMs. For each CT-condition pair, XGLASS ranks all axial slices by relevance to the queried finding, and the downstream model is evaluated only on the Top- K K selected slices. Metrics are computed over the inspected slices and compared against applying the same model to all 240 slices. Prompts, detailed inference settings and a matched-budget comparison to other slice selection methods are provided in Supplementary Sec. G . As shown in Fig. 4 , smaller XGLASS budgets consistently improve precision across MedGemma 4B [ 35 ] , Lingshu 7B [ 44 ] , and BioMedCLIP [ 47 ] , indicating that XGLASS determines disease-enriched slice subsets. This also improves F1 over inspected slices at small budgets: Top-30 improves F1 from 0.288 to 0.414 for MedGemma, from 0.327 to 0.441 for Lingshu, and from 0.235 to 0.316 for BioMedCLIP. Compared with other slice-selected subsets, XGLASS improves average Top-30 F1 over the strongest 2D selector from 0.338 to 0.390, while remaining competitive to the strongest 3D selector. Evaluating fewer slices also reduces downstream runtime, with Top-30 requiring only 12.5% of the slice-wise model calls compared with all-slice inference. This supports XGLASS as a fast pre-selection step that enriches disease-relevant slices before costly slice-wise VLM review, 2D dataset curation or similar applications.

The corresponding validation results and selection criteria are reported in Supplementary Sec. E . All ablations tables modify only one factor at a time, and are reported on the held-out test set. blocks.en: 4.4.1 Weak Supervision.
blocks.zh: 4.4.1 监督薄弱。

blocks.en: Our best training target uses segmentation-derived slice-area scores, but XGLASS can also be trained from substantially weaker annotations. We evaluate three reduced-supervision targets: SE-Binary , which marks all slices between annotated start and end positions as positive; SE-Smooth , which additionally applies Gaussian smoothing to this interval; and Rel-Rank , which uses relative slice ranking instead of dense area scores. As shown in Table 3 , reduced-supervision targets remain competitive, highlighting XGLASS’s ability to be trained from weak annotations.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion and Limitations
blocks.zh: 5. 结论和限制

blocks.en: We presented XGLASS, a lightweight disease-conditioned model that transfers aggregated CXR gaze-language priors to CT for relevance-ordered axial slice retrieval. XGLASS significantly improves Hit@5 and Hit@10 over the strongest evaluated 2D and 3D baselines while remaining computationally efficient. Downstream experiments further show that XGLASS enriches compact disease-relevant candidate sets, improves downstream classification performance, and reduces slice-wise model calls. Beyond slice selection, XGLASS illustrates how heterogeneous 2D supervision can help bridge the gap between 2D foundation models and 3D medical image analysis. Nevertheless, several limitations remain. Despite surveying publicly available CT datasets, ReXGroundingCT is the only dataset, that overlaps with the 14 REFLACX-derived disease priors, yielding only to one dataset and six shared thoracic findings for evaluation. Our downstream screening experiments provide an initial demonstration of XGLASS utility and not direct use cases; broader applications such as VQA, report generation, retrieval, and localization remain future work.
blocks.zh: 我们提出了XGLASS, 一种轻量级的疾病条件模型, 将CXR凝视语言的前身转移给CT, 用于相关的轴心回收。 XGLASS大大改进了Hit@5和Hit@10,超过了最强的评价2D和3D基线,同时保持了计算效率. 下游实验进一步表明,XGLASS丰富了紧凑的与疾病相关的候选集,改善了下游的分类性能,并减少了切片模式调用. 除了切片选择外,XGLASS还说明了多变的2D监督如何能帮助弥合2D基础模型和3D医疗图像分析之间的差距. 然而,仍然存在若干限制。 尽管对公开提供的CT数据集进行了调查,但ReXGroundingCT是唯一的数据集,它与14个REFLACX衍生疾病前科重叠,只得出一个数据集和六个共享的胸肌结果供评价. 我们的下游筛选实验初步展示了XGLASS的有用性,而不是直接使用的案例;VQA,报告生成,检索,本地化等更广泛的应用仍然是今后的工作.

blocks.en: Appendix B Disease-Conditioned Importance Maps

blocks.en: B.1 Text–Gaze Alignment
blocks.zh: B.1 文本对齐

blocks.en: To construct disease-conditioned 2D importance maps from REFLACX [ 4 ] , we jointly process the word-level transcripts and synchronized gaze recordings. For each target disease, we first detect positive (non-negated) mentions in the transcript using label-specific regular expressions together with clause-level negation handling, as described in Section 3.1 . Each detected mention defines a speech window [ t start − τ pre , t end ] [t_{\text{start}}-\tau_{\text{pre}},\,t_{\text{end}}] with a short pre-speech buffer τ pre \tau_{\text{pre}} of 2 seconds to account for anticipatory gaze. We then collect all gaze samples whose timestamps fall inside this window and project their screen coordinates onto the corresponding chest X-ray. Following the REFLACX protocol, we normalize coordinates to the chest bounding box and discard samples that fall outside this region (e.g., blink artefacts or fixations off the image). Figure 5 shows qualitative examples of the resulting text–gaze alignment for the six disease categories used in this work.
blocks.zh: 为了从REFLACX[4]构建基于疾病条件的2D重要地图,我们共同处理文字级记录和同步凝视录音. 对于每个目标疾病,我们首先在记录中检测阳性(非阴性),使用特定标签的正则表达以及条款级否定处理,如第3.1节所述。 每个检测到的引用定义了语音窗口 [t start -\\\ pre, t end] [t\ text{ start *\\\\\\ text{ pre\,\, t\ t\ text{ end} 带有一个短的预发缓冲 \ tau\ text{ pre} 2 秒的预发缓冲 \ tau\ text{ pre} 以表示预发的视线 。 然后我们收集所有目光样本 时间戳落在这个窗口里 并将其屏幕坐标投射到相应的胸部X光上 遵循REFLACX协议,我们将坐标与胸框和该区域外的丢弃样品(例如闪烁艺术品或固定图像)正常化。 图5显示了在这项工作中使用的6个疾病类别中形成文本的定性实例。

blocks.en: B.3 AP–PA Robustness of CXR Gaze Priors
blocks.zh: B.3 AP-PA CXR Gaze Presidents的强大性

blocks.en: Because REFLACX is derived from frontal chest radiographs, one potential concern is that the resulting gaze priors may depend on acquisition view. AP and PA radiographs can differ in apparent anatomy due to projection geometry, magnification, and patient positioning. We therefore stratify REFLACX sessions by MIMIC-CXR view position and construct separate AP-only and PA-only disease-conditioned gaze maps. Figures 12 and 13 compare the resulting maps for all six target findings. Despite view-dependent differences in the 2D heatmaps, the superior–inferior profiles remain similar across AP and PA views, with correlations ranging from r = 0.53 r{=}0.53 to 0.96 0.96 . Since this axis is the one used for axial slice ordering, these results support combining AP and PA sessions to obtain more stable disease-conditioned gaze priors for XGLASS.
blocks.zh: 由于REFLACX来源于前胸放射图,一个潜在的担忧是由此而来的眼睛前传可能依赖于获取视图. 由于投影几何,放大和病人定位,AP和PA的放射图在明显的解剖学上可以有所不同. 因此,我们通过MIMIC-CXR视图位置来划分REFLACX的会话,并构建单独的只限AP和仅限PA的有病凝视图. 图12和图13比较了所有六个目标结果的地图。 尽管在2D热图中视差不同,但是在AP和PA的观点中,上等-下等剖面仍然相似,其相关性从r=0.53 r{=}0.53到0.96 0.96不等. 由于这个轴是轴切点用的轴,这些结果支持结合AP会话和PA会话,为XGLASS获得更稳定的有病前视线.

blocks.en: B.4 CXR–CT Gaze Alignment
blocks.zh: B.4 CXR-CT 对齐

blocks.en: To further assess whether CXR-derived gaze priors capture transferable anatomical search patterns, we compare them with CT-ScanGaze [ 32 ] , a CT eye-tracking dataset with timestamped dictation. CT-ScanGaze contains 57 unique CT cases, but several scans have inconsistent orientation metadata or cover non-chest anatomy. We therefore performed visual quality control and excluded cases with incorrect projection geometry or non-thoracic coverage. For the remaining cases, we constructed disease-conditioned CT gaze maps analogously to the REFLACX priors: report sentences were matched to gaze by timestamp, using the same 2 s pre-speech buffer, and fixations were aggregated for the corresponding finding. These CT-ScanGaze maps provide insight into CT gaze patterns but are substantially sparser than REFLACX, with 6–23 CT cases and 244–1,215 fixations per finding (mean: 12.8 cases and 731 fixations). Figures 14 – 15 compare the resulting CT-ScanGaze maps with the REFLACX CXR priors. The 2D heatmaps differ visibly, reflecting different reading behavior in CT: radiologists often fixate a local region and scroll through adjacent axial slices, rather than scanning broadly across the frontal image as in CXR. However, the superior–inferior gaze-density profiles remain aligned across modalities, with correlations ranging from 0.65 to 0.96 for the analyzed findings. This indicates that although CT and CXR differ in traversal order and fixation dynamics, radiologists still attend to similar disease-relevant anatomical regions. Thus, the CXR-derived gaze priors encode non-arbitrary, disease-specific search patterns that can be transferred to CT and used as additional input for axial slice selection.
blocks.zh: 为了进一步评估CXR派生的凝视前传是否捕捉了可转移的解剖学搜索模式,我们将它们与CT-ScanGaze[32]进行比较,CT眼跟踪数据集带有时间标记的凹陷. CT-ScanGaze包含57个独特的CT案例,但多个扫描具有不一致的方向元数据或者覆盖了非切特解剖学. 因此,我们进行了目视质量控制,排除了投影几何或非胸膜覆盖的病例。 对于其余病例,我们构建了与REFLACX前作相似的基于疾病条件的CT凝视图:报告句子被配以时间戳来凝视,使用同样的2 s s s s speech 缓冲器,并汇总了固定来进行相应的发现. 这些CT-ScanGaze地图提供了CT凝视模式的洞察力,但比REFLACX少得多,每个发现有6至23个CT病例和244至1,215个固定病例(指12.8个病例和731个固定病例)。 图14 – 15 将由此产生的CT-ScanGaze地图与REFLACX CXR前作作比较. 2D热映射明显不同,反映了CT中不同的读取行为:放射学家经常固定一个局部区域并通过相邻的轴切片来滚动,而不是像CXR那样在正面图像上作大扫描. 然而,在各种模式中,优等-低等-视星等密度分布仍然一致,分析结果的相关程度从0.65到0.96不等。 这表明,虽然CT和CXR在转录顺序和固定动力学上有所不同,但放射学家仍然关注类似的与疾病有关的解剖区域. 因此,从CXR得到的凝视前缀编码了非任意的,针对疾病的搜索模式,可以被转移到CT,并用作轴切片选择的额外输入.

blocks.en: Appendix C CT Dataset and Volume Projections
blocks.zh: 附录 CT 数据集和数量预测

blocks.en: C.1 Dataset Selection
blocks.zh: C.1 数据集选择

blocks.en: To evaluate how effectively our disease-specific eye-tracking priors transfer from CXR to CT, we require a CT dataset that (i) provides report text and findings aligned with individual volumes, and (ii) contains findings that can be reliably matched to our REFLACX-derived disease-specific importance maps. As discussed in Section 3.2 , ReXGroundingCT [ 3 ] is, to our knowledge, the only large-scale CT dataset that satisfies both criteria. Because this dataset will also be used to train XGLASS, each disease category must be supported by a sufficient number of CT studies. We therefore exclude any finding category with fewer than 100 matching CTs. As shown in Figure 7 and Figure 8 , only six of the 14 REFLACX-defined categories reach this threshold in our standardized 240-slice ReXGroundingCT subset introduced in Section 3.2 , and we consequently restrict our experiments to these six categories.
blocks.zh: 为了评价我们针对特定疾病的目光跟踪前科从CXR到CT的转移如何有效,我们需要一个CT数据集,以便(一) 提供与各个卷相一致的报告文本和结果,(二) 包含能够可靠地与我们REFLACX产生的疾病特定重要性图相匹配的结果。 如第3.2节所讨论,据我们所知,ReXGroundingCT[3]是唯一符合两个标准的大型CT数据集。 由于这个数据集也会被用来训练XGLASS,因此每个疾病类别都必须有足够的CT研究支持. 因此,我们排除了任何低于100个对应CT的发现类别。 如图7和图8所示,在3.2节中引入的我们的标准240-sice ReXGroundingCT子集中,REFLACX定义的14个类别中只有6个达到这一阈值,因此,我们的实验仅限于这6个类别。

blocks.en: C.2 Training Dataset and Splits
blocks.zh: C.2 培训数据集和组合

blocks.en: We use an 80/10/10 CT-volume-level train–validation–test split of the standardized 240-slice ReXGroundingCT subset, with no volume overlap between partitions and all findings from each CT retained in the same split. This yields 2,514/306/316 CT–finding cases for training/validation/testing, respectively, totaling 3,136 cases across six categories: Lung nodule or mass (1,096), Groundglass opacity (925), Atelectasis (412), High lung volume (301), Consolidation (284), and Pleural abnormality (118), as shown in Fig. 8 . The disease distribution in our ReXGroundingCT subset is markedly imbalanced across our six categories. However the best performing model did not apply class-balancing or reweighting (e.g., oversampling, inverse-frequency sampling, focal/weighted losses), because the most prevalent class, lung nodule or mass , is also the hardest to localize due to its small size, variable location, and sparse slice extent. This choice is supported by the disease-specific results in Table 2 of the main paper, where XGLASS improves across all disease categories, and by the loss-function ablation in Sec. F.5 , where reweighted objectives do not improve small-finding and overall retrieval performance.
blocks.zh: 我们使用一个80/10/10的CT-量级列车 - 验证 - 测试分拆标准240-切片 ReXGroundingCT子集,分区之间没有数量重叠,每个CT的所有结果都保留在同一分解中. 这样,培训/鉴定/测试的CT调查案件分别达到2 514/306/316起,共有6个类别的3 136起: 如图8所显示,肺结核或质量(1 096个)、地镜不透明(925个)、Atelectasis(412个)、高肺体积(301个)、综合(284个)和Pleural异常(118个)。 我们的ReXGroundingCT子集中的疾病分布在我们六个类别中明显不平衡。 然而,最佳表现模式没有采用类平衡或再加权(例如,过度取样、反频取样、焦/加权损失),因为最常见的类别,即肺结核或质量,也因其体积小、位置多变和切片范围稀疏而难以定位。 这一选择得到了主要文件表2中针对具体疾病的结果的支持,XGLASS在所有疾病类别中都有所改进,而Sec.F.5.中则有功能丧失症,而重新加权的目标并不能改善小发现和总体检索性能.

blocks.en: C.3 CT Volume Projections
blocks.zh: C.3 CT 量预测

blocks.en: For XGLASS, each 3D chest CT volume is converted into a 2D coronal intensity projection that lives in the same domain as our disease-conditioned importance maps, as explained in Section 3.2. Formally, we project along the anterior–posterior axis and aggregate attenuation values along each ray using an operator A A (Beer–Lambert or average-intensity), yielding a coronal image P A ​ ( u , v ) P_{A}(u,v) for each volume. In the main experiments we focus on two projection families: (i) a physically motivated Beer-Lambert projection that mimics x-ray transmission, and (ii) average-intensity projections (AIP) combined with standard CT windowings. For AIP we consider three clinical window settings: a lung window, a soft-tissue window, and a wide window spanning a broad Hounsfield range. As discussed in Section 3.2 and ablated in Section 4.4.2, Beer-Lambert provides slightly better global ranking (AUC, Spearman), whereas AIP with a wide window offers the best early retrieval utility (Hit@K). Figure 9 illustrates how a single CT scan appears under these different projection choices, highlighting how windowing and projection type emphasize complementary structures (e.g., parenchyma in the lung window vs. mediastinum and pleural surfaces under broader windows).
blocks.zh: 对于XGLASS来说,每个3D胸口CT体积被转换为2D的日冕强度投影,它和我们的疾病条件重要性图生活在同一个域中,第3.2节对此有解释. 在形式上,我们使用一个操作员A(比尔-朗伯特或平均强度),在每道射线上沿前-后轴投影并显示总衰减值,得出每卷的冠状图像PA(u,v)PQA(u,v)。 在主要实验中,我们侧重于两个投影家族:(一) 模仿X射线传播的物理动力的啤酒-兰伯特投影,和(二) 平均强度预测(AIP)与标准的CT窗口结合. 对于AIP来说,我们考虑三个临床窗口设置:一个肺窗,一个软组织窗口,以及一个横跨广泛胡恩斯菲尔德范围的宽窗. 如第3.2节所讨论,并在第4.4.2节所删节,啤酒-兰伯特在全球的排名略好一些(AUC, Spearman),而具有宽窗口的AIP则提供了最好的早期检索工具(Hit@K)。 图9说明了在这些不同的投影选择下,单一CT扫描是如何出现的,突出显示窗口和投影类型如何强调互补结构(如:肺窗中的parenchyma与更宽的窗口下的中子和胸膜表面).

blocks.en: C.4 Gaze-Prior Blending Strength
blocks.zh: C.4. 迷宫-先入为主

blocks.en: In XGLASS, the 2D CT projection and the disease-specific REFLACX gaze importance map are combined by injecting the normalized gaze heatmap H d ​ ( u , v ) H_{d}(u,v) into the red channel inside the chest bounding box using a blending coefficient α ∈ [ 0 , 1 ] \alpha\in[0,1] . Here, α = 0 \alpha=0 corresponds to the CT-only input, whereas larger values increase the contribution of the disease-conditioned gaze prior in the fused representation. Figure 11 illustrates the qualitative effect of varying α \alpha for representative CT studies. The quantitative test-set ablation of α \alpha is reported in Sec. 4.4.3 of the main paper. The final value α = 0.75 \alpha{=}0.75 was selected on the validation split, as described in Sec. E .
blocks.zh: 在XGLASS中,2D CT投影和疾病特异性REFLACX视星等图通过将正态的视热图H d (u, v)H_{d} (u,v) 注射入胸框内的红色通道,使用混合系数α → [0, 1]\ alpha\ in [0, 1]. 这里,α = 0\alpha = 0对应 CT 仅输入,而较大的值则会增加在被熔化的表示中前的有病凝视作用. 图11显示了不同α-α对有代表性的CT研究的质量影响。 主论文第4.4.3节报告了α-α的定量测试-集衰减。 如Sec. E. 所述,在验证分拆上选定了 α = 0.75\alpha = 0.75的最后值。

blocks.en: F.3 Gaze-Only and CT-Derived Prior Ablations
blocks.zh: F.3. 仅限Gaze-Oly和CT-Derived Performation案

blocks.en:
We further analyze the role of disease-conditioned priors in XGLASS by comparing transferred CXR gaze priors with empirical CT abnormality-location priors. First, we evaluate the CXR gaze prior alone by averaging each disease-specific gaze map along the left–right axis, interpolating the resulting superior–inferior profile to 240 axial positions, and ranking slices by profile intensity. Second, we construct an empirical CT location prior using only train+val labels by averaging slice-presence vectors for each disease category and applying the resulting fixed category-specific prior to all corresponding test cases. Third, we replace the gaze map in XGLASS with this CT-derived prior converted into a synthetic heatmap and fuse it with the CT projection in the same way as the gaze heatmap.
Since this CT prior is computed from train+val ground-truth slice-presence targets from the same CT dataset distribution, it represents an empirical average lesion-location prior for each abnormality. In contrast, the gaze prior is transferred from CXR eye-tracking and does not use CT lesion-location statistics; instead, it captures radiologist visual search patterns that include both observed abnormality regions and plausible candidate regions inspected for each finding. In contrast, the CT-derived prior is less reliable when abnormalities occur in rare locations, whereas the broader radiologist search patterns encoded by the gaze prior can still overlap these regions, supporting the use of gaze over CT derived location priors. Table 10 shows that CT location statistics are informative: the CT location prior alone achieves the best Hit@1 and Spearman correlation. However, the full gaze-guided XGLASS model achieves the best AUC and performs substantially better for utility-centric top- K K retrieval metrics, improving Hit@10 from 0.453 0.453 to 0.563 0.563 and Hit@20 from 0.522 0.522 to 0.693 0.693 compared with the CT location prior alone. Injecting the CT-derived prior into XGLASS also improves over CT-only input at Hit@10 ( 0.535 0.535 vs. 0.468 0.468 ). Nevertheless, gaze-guided XGLASS remains stronger at Hit@10 and Hit@20, indicating that the transferred radiologist gaze prior provides complementary information beyond average CT lesion-frequency statistics, which improves the slice selection performance especially for higher K K . We additionally stratify test samples by their typicality under the train+val CT location prior, defined as the average CT-prior score over the ground-truth positive slices of each test sample. In low-typicality cases, where the empirical CT prior assigns low probability to the true lesion region, the CT location prior drops sharply to Hit@10 of 0.151 0.151 . In contrast, the CXR gaze prior alone remains stronger at Hit@10 of 0.330 0.330 , while full XGLASS reaches Hit@10 of 0.358 0.358 and Hit@20 of 0.528 0.528 . This suggests that empirical CT priors primarily capture common dataset-specific lesion locations, whereas radiologist gaze priors cover broader disease-specific search regions. Combined with patient-specific CT projection evidence, this leads to more robust disease-conditioned slice prioritization than static location priors alone.

我们进一步分析疾病条件前科在XGLASS的作用,将转移的CXR视前科与经验性的CT异常-位置前科进行比较. 首先,我们通过对左-右轴上每个疾病特有目视图的平均值来评价CXR的目视,将由此形成的上等-下等相图插到240个轴地上,并按目视强度进行分级。 其次,我们先用列车+val标签来构建一个经验性CT位置,方法是在每种疾病类别中平均使用切片活性载体,并在所有相应试验病例之前应用由此产生的特定固定类别。 第三,我们把XGLASS的凝视图换成这个CT先出自的被转换成合成热图,并以和凝视热图相同的方式将它与CT投影相接.
由于这个CT前身是从同一CT数据集分布的列车+val地平面-真能片-存在目标中计算出来的,它代表了每次异常发生前的经验平均损伤位置. 相形之下,前视从CXR眼跟踪转出,不使用CT损伤位置统计;相反,它捕捉到放射学家的视觉搜索模式,既包括观察到的异常地段,也包括对每项发现进行检查的可信候选地段。 相形之下,当异常发生于稀有地点时,CT先导的可靠性较低,而由前导视所编码的更广泛的放射学家搜索模式仍然可以与这些区域相重叠,支持使用对CT后导位置前导视. 表10显示CT位置统计信息丰富:之前仅CT位置就实现了最佳Hit@1和斯皮尔曼关联. 然而,全视向制导的XGLAS模型达到了最好的AUC,并且对以功用为中心的顶端-K K检索度量衡的性能大有改进,比起之前的CT位置,Hit@10从0.453 0453提高到0.563 0.563;Hit@20从0.522 0.522提高到0.693 0.693。 在Hit@10(0.535 0.535 vs.0.468 0 468)上将先前生成的CT注入XGLASS也比仅输入CT有所改进. 然而,在Hit@10和Hit@20上,目视制导的XGLASS仍然更强大,表明被转移的放射学家先前的目视提供了超出平均CT损伤频率统计的补充信息,这提高了切片选择的性能,尤其是对更高的K K. 此外,我们还根据试验样品在列车+val CT车站位置下的典型程度,对试验样品进行分层,即每个试验样品地面-真实正切片上的平均CT-先得分。 在低常态的情况下,经验性CT前传将低概率分配给真正的损伤区域时,CT前传位置会急剧下降到Hit@10,0.151 0.151. 相形之下,CXR先前的视线在0.330 0.330的Hit@10上仍然较强;而完整的XGLASS则达到0.358 0.358的Hit@10和0.528 0.528的Hit@20。 这表明经验性CT前科主要捕捉到常见的数据集特异性损伤地点,而放射学家的目光前科则覆盖更广泛的特定疾病搜索区域. 与患者特有的CT投影证据相结合,这导致比仅静态地点更强有力的基于疾病条件的片段优先排序。

blocks.en: F.4 Robustness to Gaze-Prior Perturbations
blocks.zh: F.4 强力对付加兹先发制人

blocks.en: To test whether XGLASS depends on exact pixel-level alignment of the transferred gaze prior, we first measured coarse anatomical alignment between CXR-derived priors and CT projections using lung and heart layouts, obtaining a lungs+heart centroid error of 16.2 px and an average symmetric surface distance of 11.6 px; for lungs alone, the corresponding errors were 8.8 px and 8.0 px. We then perturb the disease-conditioned heatmap at test time while keeping the CT projection unchanged. Table 11 shows that random spatial shifts, additive noise, and left–right heatmap flips only mildly affect performance, supporting that XGLASS uses the gaze map as a broad anatomical search prior, that is robust to minor perturbations, rather than an exact lesion-location mask.
blocks.zh: 为了测试XGLASS是否依赖于之前转移的视线的精确像素级对齐,我们首先用肺和心平面布局测量出CXR出自前传和CT预测之间的粗解剖线对齐,得到的肺+心心心心离子误差为16.2px,平均对称地表距离为11.6px;仅肺本身,相应的误差为8.8px和8.0px. 然后在试验时扰动疾病条件下的热图,同时保持CT投影不变. 表11显示,随机空间变化、添加性噪音和左-右热图翻转只会轻而易举地影响性能,支持XGLASS将视星等图作为广泛的解剖前搜索,它坚固到轻微扰动,而不是精确的损伤位置口罩.

blocks.en: F.5 Loss Function Ablation

blocks.en: Abnormalities vary substantially in spatial extent, e.g., consolidations often cover larger regions than lung nodules. We therefore compare four training objectives while keeping all other settings fixed: MSE regresses the normalized slice-area target, Focal treats each slice as positive or negative and emphasizes difficult cases, Slice-bal. MSE gives equal aggregate weight to positive and negative slices within each CT, preventing scans with many positive slices from dominating the loss, and Size-wt. MSE inversely weights positive-slice errors by the total lesion size in each CT, reducing the contribution of spatially extensive lesions. Table 12 shows that MSE gives the strongest overall retrieval-ranking trade-off, with the best Hit@1 and Hit@10 and tied-best Hit@5. We further stratify the same ablation by finding extent. Test cases are split into small, medium, and large tertiles by total ground-truth slice-area mass, corresponding to average extents of 5.6, 14.7, and 52.4 positive slices, respectively.
blocks.zh: 异常程度在空间范围上差异很大,例如,合并往往覆盖大于肺结核的区域。 因此,我们比较四个培训目标,同时固定所有其他设置: MSE 使常规切片区目标倒退,Cacer 将每个切片视为正或负,并强调困难的病例 Slic-bal. MSE在每个CT内对正负切片给予等同的总分权重,防止了用许多正切片来支配损失的扫描和大小-wt. MSE反向地将正切片误差按每个CT的总损伤大小来加权,减少空间广度损伤的成因. 表12显示,MSE给出了最强的总体检索级取舍,最佳Hit@1和Hit@10和捆绑-最佳Hit@5. 我们进一步通过寻找范围来划分同样的范围。 试验病例按地面真实切片面积总质量分为小、中和大三角形,平均分别为5.6、14.7和52.4正切片。

blocks.en: Table 13 shows that MSE is strongest for small sparse findings across retrieval metrics, whereas Focal and Slice-bal. MSE mainly improve medium or large findings. Although the reweighted objectives were intended to improve small-lesion retrieval, they appear to amplify the instability of very sparse positive targets: for small findings, only a few slices are labeled relevant and the corresponding projection evidence is often weak, so upweighting these slices can emphasize case-specific noise. In contrast, MSE preserves the continuous slice-area target and provides a smoother ranking signal, making it the most stable default objective.

blocks.en: G.2 3D Baseline Implementation Details
blocks.zh: G.2 3D 基线执行细节

blocks.en: For the 3D Merlin + MLP baseline, we follow the CT preparation used by Merlin [ 6 ] : full CT volumes are resampled to 1.5 × 1.5 × 3.0 1.5{\times}1.5{\times}3.0 mm spacing and resized to 160 × 224 × 224 160{\times}224{\times}224 before encoding. The Merlin encoder is kept frozen and used to precompute one 2048-dimensional volume embedding per CT. We then train a disease-conditioned MLP on ReXGroundingCT to regress the same 240-dimensional slice-relevance target as XGLASS. The MLP uses a 32-dimensional disease embedding concatenated with the Merlin feature, followed by two 512-unit hidden layers with ReLU activations and dropout 0.1 0.1 , and a final linear layer producing 240 slice scores. The MLP is trained with AdamW, learning rate 10 − 3 10^{-3} , weight decay 10 − 4 10^{-4} , batch size 64, and the best checkpoint is selected on the validation loss. Including embedding precomputation, the full Merlin baseline required approximately 6 hours on an A100 GPU. For the 3D U-Net baseline, we train a compact 3D U-Net from scratch on ReXGroundingCT. Full CT volumes are resampled to 1.25 1.25 mm isotropic spacing and resized to 160 × 224 × 224 160{\times}224{\times}224 . The encoder uses 3D convolutional blocks with base width 16 and instance normalization. To obtain slice scores, the final feature maps are averaged over the in-plane dimensions, interpolated to 240 axial positions, concatenated with a 32-dimensional disease embedding, and passed through a slice-regression head. The model is trained with AdamW, learning rate 10 − 4 10^{-4} , weight decay 10 − 4 10^{-4} , batch size 16, dropout 0.1 0.1 , and the best checkpoint is selected on the validation loss and Training to the selected checkpoint required approximately 22 hours on an A100 GPU. Both 3D baselines are therefore substantially more compute-intensive to train than XGLASS, which trains in under 10 minutes on a single RTX 4080.
blocks.zh: 对于3D Merlin + MLP 基线,我们遵循Merlin 使用的 CT 制备 [6] : 全CT卷被重印为1.5×1.5×3.0 1.5×时×1.5×时×3.0相距3.0毫米,并被重印为160×224×224相距160×224相距160×224相距224相距. 在编码之前。 默林编码器被保持被冷冻,并用于预先计算出每CT一个2048维的体积嵌入. 然后在ReXGaturningCT上训练一个有疾病条件的MLP,以倒置与XGLASS相同的240维切片相关目标. MLP使用与默林特征相融合的32维嵌入式疾病,后有2个512个单元的隐藏层,并有ReLU活化和放出0.1分,最后的线性层产生240分切分. MLP训练有AdamW,学习率 10 − 3 10^{-3},体重衰减 10 − 4 10^{-4},批量尺寸 64,在验证损失上选择最佳检查点. 包括嵌入预计算,整个梅林基线需要大约6小时的A100GPU. 对于3D U-Net基线,我们从零开始在REXGaturningCT上训练一个紧凑的3D U-Net. 全CT卷被重印为1.25 1.25毫米同位素相距并被调整为160×224×224 160×times}224×times}224. 编码器使用基宽为16并实现例常化的3D分化块. 为了得到切片分数,最终的地物图被平均地取在平面维度上,插入到240个轴位置上,并用一个32维的疾病嵌入来相接,并经过一个切片后退头. 该型号由AdamW,学习率10 - 4 10-QQ-4},体重衰减10 - 4 10-Q-4},批量尺寸16,辍学0.1 选取最佳检查点,对选定的检查点进行验证损失和培训,需要大约22小时的A100 GPU。 因此,两个3D基线对训练的计算强度都大大高于XGLASS,后者在一列RTX 4080上行驶不到10分钟.

blocks.en: G.3 Slice-wise Medical VLM Screening
blocks.zh: G.3 切片医学 VLM 筛选

blocks.en: We evaluate google/medgemma-4b-it [ 35 ] and lingshu-medical-mllm/Lingshu-7B [ 44 ] using the same disease-conditioned binary screening task. Motivated by CT vision-language transfer work that maps complementary HU windows to RGB channels to expose different tissue contrasts [ 30 ] , the main-paper experiments use a pseudo-RGB representation with wide/lung, soft-tissue, and mediastinal/fluid windows assigned to separate channels. As an input-rendering sensitivity analysis, we additionally evaluate a standard wide-window representation ( − 1024 -1024 to 1024 1024 HU) and replicated across all RGB channels. This alternative setting shows the same trend: XGLASS Top- K K preselection improves F1 over all-slice screening, with the strongest gains at small budgets (e.g., Top-30 F1 of 0.414 for MedGemma and 0.441 for Lingshu). Thus, the downstream benefit of XGLASS is consistent across CT slice renderings. Both models receive the same system and user instructions:
blocks.zh: 我们利用同样的疾病条件二进制筛选任务,评估谷歌/medgemma-4b-it[35]和lingshu-medical-mllm/Lingshu-7B[44]。 由CT视觉-语言传导工作推动,将互补的HU窗口映射到RGB频道以暴露出不同的组织对比度[30],主论文实验使用伪RGB代表作,并有宽/隆,软-tissue,介质/流体窗口被分配到单独的频道. 作为输入-传递灵敏度分析,我们额外评价了标准的宽窗口代表(−1024-1024至1024-1024 HU),并在所有RGB频道复制. 这一替代设置显示了同样的趋势: XGLAS Top-K K预选比全片片筛选改进了F1,在小预算上收益最大(如:MedGemma的Top-30 F1为0.414,Lingshu为0.441). 因此,XGLASS的下游好处在CT切片渲染上是一致的. 两种模式都得到同样的系统和用户指示:

blocks.en: System: You are an expert thoracic radiologist. Evaluate only the queried finding on one axial chest CT slice. User: Are there clear visual signs of {finding} in this axial CT slice? Ignore other abnormalities. If the queried finding is not visible in this slice, answer no. Return only one short line, with no explanation: Answer: yes or Answer: no .

blocks.en: We use deterministic decoding and parse the response as yes, no, or unknown; no unknown responses occurred in the reported MedGemma and Lingshu evaluation. MedGemma is evaluated in bfloat16 without quantization, while Lingshu is loaded with 4-bit NF4 quantization and bfloat16 computation due to memory requirements. Predictions are generated independently for every slice and cached, allowing identical predictions to be evaluated on either all 240 slices or XGLASS-selected Top- K K subsets. Precision, recall, and F1 are computed only over the inspected slices.
blocks.zh: 我们使用决定性的解码方法,并将答复解码为是、否或未知;在所报告的MedGemma和Lingshu评价中,没有出现未知的答复。 MeDGemma在bfloat16中不进行定量评价,而Lingshu则被装入了4位NF4定量和bfloat16由于内存要求而进行计算. 每个切片和缓存都独立生成预测,可以对所有240个切片或XGLASS所选Top-K子集进行相同的预测评价. 精度、召回和F1只计算在检查的片子上。

blocks.en: G.4 Downstream Slice Selection Comparison
blocks.zh: G.4 下游切片选择比较

blocks.en: We further analyze how slice selection affects downstream screening when the number of inspected slices is fixed. For each CT–finding pair, we vary only the ranking used to choose the Top- K K inspected slices, while keeping the downstream slice-wise predictions unchanged. This isolates the effect of slice selection from stochasticity or repeated downstream model calls. We compare XGLASS with Random selection, Vote-MI, BioMedCLIP retrieval, and the two 3D-native selectors, 3D Merlin + MLP and 3D U-Net. BioMedCLIP retrieval is evaluated as a selector for MedGemma and Lingshu, but omitted from the BioMedCLIP downstream panel to avoid selecting and classifying slices with the same image–text similarity model. Figure 10 shows that selector choice strongly affects low-budget screening, especially at K = 30 K{=}30 and K = 60 K{=}60 . XGLASS consistently outperforms the other 2D selectors under matched slice budgets, while the 3D selectors are competitive and sometimes achieve the highest downstream F1 for specific model–budget combinations. Notably, XGLASS remains close to these volumetric selectors despite using only a lightweight 2D projection, and outperforms them for Lingshu at K = 30 K{=}30 , 60 60 , and 180 180 . This suggests that the disease-conditioned XGLASS ranking transfers effectively to downstream screening, narrowing much of the gap to more expensive 3D-native selection.
blocks.zh: 我们进一步分析在检查的切片数量固定时,切片选择如何影响下游筛选。 对于每对CT-调查,我们只改变用于选择Top-K检查的切片的排名,同时保持下游切片预测不变。 这隔离了切片选择的效果与分色或重复的下游模型调用. 我们比较 XGLASS 和 Random selection, Vote-MI, BioMedCLIP reference, 以及两个 3D 本地选择器, 3D Merlin + MLP 和 3D U-Net. BioMedCLIP reference 被评价为 MedGemma 和 Lingshu 的 选择器, 但省略了 BioMedCLIP 下游面板, 以避免选择和分类切片与 同一图像-文本相似性模型。 图10显示,选择者对低预算筛选的影响很大,特别是在K=30K{=}30和K=60K{=}60。 XGLASS在相匹配的切片预算下一贯优于其他2D选择器,而3D选择器则具有竞争力,有时在特定模型-预算组合上达到最高下游F1. 值得注意的是,XGLASS仍然接近这些体积选择器,尽管它只使用了一个轻量级的2D投影,在K = 30 K{=}30,60 60,180 180 上,它的表现超过了它们. 这表明以疾病为条件的XGLASS排名有效转移到下游筛选,将大部分差距缩小为更昂贵的3D-本土选择.

blocks.en: G.5 Downstream Computational Cost
blocks.zh: G.5 下游计算费用

blocks.en: Applying the downstream models to all 240 slices of one CT requires approximately 1.40 1.40 s for BioMedCLIP, 154.91 154.91 s for MedGemma, and 267.83 267.83 s for Lingshu on a single NVIDIA RTX 4080. XGLASS requires only 0.025 0.025 s per finding ( 0.150 0.150 s per CT) to rank the complete volume and allows the downstream model to inspect a smaller, disease-enriched subset. At Top-30, including XGLASS preselection, the corresponding per-CT runtimes decrease to approximately 0.20 0.20 s, 19.39 19.39 s, and 33.51 33.51 s, respectively. Thus, XGLASS reduces downstream runtime by 85.7 85.7 – 87.5 % 87.5\% while simultaneously improving F1 at the smaller slice budget, showing that preselection improves both computational efficiency and downstream screening performance.
blocks.zh: 将下游模型应用到一个CT的所有240个切片上,需要约1.40 1.40 s的BioMedCLIP,154.91 154.91 s的MedGemma,以及267.83 267.83 s的Lingshu在一个单 NVIDIA RTX 4080上. XGLASS只需要0.025 0.025 s的每次发现(0.150. 0.15 s每CT)来排列完整的体积,并允许下游模型检查一个较小的多病子集. 在Top-30,包括XGLASS预选赛中,对应的每CT跑出时间分别下降到了约0.20.0秒,19.39 19.39秒和33.51 33.51秒. 因此,XGLASS将下游运行时间减少了85.785.7 — — 87.5%87.5 — — — 同时在较小的切片预算上改进了F1,表明预选提高了计算效率和下游筛选性能.
